title: BCM Internal RAM Fault
shortDescription: Body control module internal RAM read/write fault.
fullDescription: Self-test of the BCM volatile memory has failed during power-up. Random body system misbehavior, lost personalization, and inability to clear codes are common.
safetyImpact: Body module faults rarely affect drivability directly but can disable lighting, locks, or wipers needed for safe operation.

causes.cause: Module not programmed to VIN after replacement
Damaged power, ground, or CAN wiring

fixSteps.title: Verify Power and Ground
fixSteps.instruction: Test BCM main feed and grounds with a 10A load. Voltage drops should be under 0.2 V.

fixSteps.title: Scan All Modules
fixSteps.instruction: Read DTCs network-wide. A bus-off or wake fault often originates in another module that the BCM is reporting.

fixSteps.title: Reprogram or Configure
fixSteps.instruction: If the module was recently replaced, perform OEM programming and as-built configuration before further diagnosis.

fixSteps.title: Replace BCM
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the BCM only after wiring, programming, and battery health are verified. Code to VIN after install.

faq.q: Will disconnecting the battery clear this?
faq.a: Sometimes intermittent codes clear, but persistent BCM faults return after the next drive cycle until repaired.

faq.q: Do I need a dealer to program a BCM?
faq.a: Most modern BCMs require OEM-level scan tools or an aftermarket J2534 setup with an OEM subscription.

title: Headlamp Low Beam Left Open
shortDescription: Left low-beam headlamp circuit open.
fullDescription: The lighting control module has detected no current draw on the left low-beam output, indicating a burned-out bulb, broken connector, or open wiring.
safetyImpact: Inoperative headlights at night greatly reduce visibility and may make the vehicle illegal to drive after dark.

fixSteps.title: Visual Bulb Check
fixSteps.instruction: Activate headlights and confirm which bulb is out. Replace burned-out halogens; LED units are usually serviced as assemblies.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Connector
fixSteps.instruction: Check the headlamp connector for melting, corrosion, or backed-out pins. Repair or replace pigtail as needed.

fixSteps.title: Test Module Output
fixSteps.instruction: Backprobe the lighting control module output and verify commanded voltage with a scope or DMM.

fixSteps.title: Calibrate Adaptive System
fixSteps.instruction: After repair on AFS or leveling, perform aim calibration with the scan tool and an aiming target.

faq.q: Why does the warning come back after a new bulb?
faq.a: If the connector has high resistance or the module is detecting cold current draw, replacing the bulb alone will not clear it.

faq.q: Can I bypass the leveling motor?
faq.a: Not safely. Beams aimed too high blind oncoming traffic and may fail inspection.

title: Front Wiper Motor Park Switch
shortDescription: Front wiper motor park switch input fault.
fullDescription: The wiper motor park signal is not seen at the expected position, leaving wipers stopped mid-windshield or running continuously.
safetyImpact: Inoperative wipers or washers in rain or snow can quickly reduce visibility to unsafe levels.

causes.cause: Failed wiper motor or park switch
Broken wires at tailgate or cowl
Washer pump seized or fluid low

fixSteps.title: Verify Operation
fixSteps.instruction: Cycle wiper switch through all positions and listen for motor response. Note which speeds work.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Hinge Wiring
fixSteps.instruction: On rear wipers, check the harness in the tailgate boot for broken conductors. Repair with solder and heat-shrink.

fixSteps.title: Test Motor and Pump
fixSteps.instruction: Apply battery voltage directly to motor or pump leads to confirm operation, then test the BCM output.

fixSteps.title: Clean or Replace Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: For rain sensor faults, clean the windshield gel pad or replace the sensor and recalibrate.

faq.q: Why do my wipers park crooked?
faq.a: The wiper linkage may have slipped on the motor shaft, or the park switch is reporting the wrong position.

faq.q: Can I drive with no rear wiper?
faq.a: Yes, but rear visibility in rain and snow is reduced. Repair before winter conditions.

title: Driver Frontal Deployment Loop
shortDescription: Driver frontal airbag deployment loop resistance.
fullDescription: The SRS module measures resistance of the driver frontal squib through the clockspring. A reading outside the calibrated window sets this code and inhibits deployment.
safetyImpact: An SRS fault may prevent airbag or pretensioner deployment in a crash, eliminating critical occupant protection.

fixSteps.title: Disable SRS Safely
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect the battery, wait the manufacturer-specified discharge time, and only then unplug airbag connectors. SRS work is hazardous if shortcuts are taken.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Connectors
fixSteps.instruction: Check yellow SRS connectors at clockspring, under seats, and at curtain anchors. Reseat and confirm shorting bar release.

fixSteps.title: Measure Squib Resistance
fixSteps.instruction: Only with an SRS-rated tester, measure squib resistance against specification. Never use a standard ohmmeter on a live squib.

fixSteps.title: Replace Component
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the affected airbag, pretensioner, or clockspring with OEM parts. Reconnect, restore power, and clear codes with a scan tool.

faq.q: Is it safe to keep driving with the airbag light on?
faq.a: Driving is mechanically safe, but airbags may not deploy in a crash. Repair as soon as possible.

faq.q: Can I clear the SRS light without a scan tool?
faq.a: No. SRS codes are stored in non-volatile memory and require a scan tool to clear after the fault is corrected.

shortDescription: Passenger side curtain or seat-side airbag loop fault.
fullDescription: Same condition as driver side, applied to the right side curtain or seat-side airbag circuit.
safetyImpact: An SRS fault may prevent airbag or pretensioner deployment in a crash, eliminating critical occupant protection.

fixSteps.title: Disable SRS Safely
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect the battery, wait the manufacturer-specified discharge time, and only then unplug airbag connectors. SRS work is hazardous if shortcuts are taken.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Connectors
fixSteps.instruction: Check yellow SRS connectors at clockspring, under seats, and at curtain anchors. Reseat and confirm shorting bar release.

fixSteps.title: Measure Squib Resistance
fixSteps.instruction: Only with an SRS-rated tester, measure squib resistance against specification. Never use a standard ohmmeter on a live squib.

fixSteps.title: Replace Component
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the affected airbag, pretensioner, or clockspring with OEM parts. Reconnect, restore power, and clear codes with a scan tool.

faq.q: Is it safe to keep driving with the airbag light on?
faq.a: Driving is mechanically safe, but airbags may not deploy in a crash. Repair as soon as possible.

faq.q: Can I clear the SRS light without a scan tool?

title: Driver Mirror Motor Vertical
shortDescription: Driver power mirror vertical motor circuit fault.
fullDescription: Open, short, or excessive current detected on the driver mirror tilt motor. The mirror cannot move up/down by switch.
safetyImpact: Mirror faults rarely affect safe driving directly but can reduce visibility in cold or wet weather when defrost is needed.

causes.cause: Worn motor brushes or stripped gear

symptoms: Mirror does not move on one axis
Memory recall does not return to saved position

fixSteps.title: Test Switch Inputs
fixSteps.instruction: With a scan tool, view mirror switch states for each direction. Confirm the input reaches the door module.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Door Hinge Wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Open the door fully and inspect the harness boot for broken wires. Repair with solder and heat-shrink.

fixSteps.title: Bench-Test Mirror Assembly
fixSteps.instruction: Apply battery voltage to motor leads at the connector and confirm motor function. Replace mirror glass or assembly as needed.

fixSteps.title: Calibrate Memory
fixSteps.instruction: After repair, use the scan tool or driver memory procedure to relearn mirror positions for each driver profile.

faq.q: Can I replace just the mirror glass?
faq.a: If the heater is the only fault, yes. Motor or fold issues usually require replacing the housing assembly.

faq.q: Does the mirror need programming after replacement?
faq.a: Memory mirrors typically require an initialization sweep so the module learns the end stops; a scan tool or door switch sequence handles this.
